newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends up on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends up on short-covering.

text.p: Hong Kong's gold market ended a shade higher on Thursday from the New York close, buoyed by short-covering, dealers and traders said.
Sentiment remained bullish despite thinly traded volumes, with gold seen testing $384.50-385.00 per ounce, gold sources said.
Hong Kong's bullion market saw very slight selling interest from traders on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) as the yen weakened during morning trade, gold dealers said.
Some local professionals had earlier taken short positions, anticipating the sales from Japan, but were disappointed at the small volumes, a bullion source at an international bank said.
Local professionals covered their positions in later trade, pushing the market up slightly, gold sources said.
Physical demand has slipped with the rise in prices, gold dealers said.
One precious metals dealer said gold bar supplies in Hong Kong territory had tightened slightly as physical traders stemmed their gold imports, anticipating reduced demand on higher prices.
Some buying interest from Swiss customers seen on Wednesday had disappeared by Thursday, one trader said.
A local player was heard selling a small amount of gold at $370 per ounce as a hedge in early trade.
"I've made a nifty profit, too bad it was such a small amount," the buyer said.
Gold would remain range bound between $382.50-384.50, bullion traders said.
Bullion ended at US$383.80/384.30 an ounce against New York's US$383.60/384.10 close on Wednesday.
Local gold ended HK$2 lower at HK$3,536 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to -0.10 on Thursday, from its previous fix of -5.00.
